title: Cullen Skink
subtitle: Scottish smoked haddock and potato soup
excerpt: A thick, creamy Scottish soup from the fishing village of Cullen: smoked haddock poached in milk with potatoes and onion, then flaked back into the smoky, silky broth. Simple, sustaining, and deeply good.

recipe.sourceNotes: Cullen skink takes its name from the Moray Firth town of Cullen, where the dish originated, and the Scottish Gaelic word skink, meaning a shin or knuckle of beef, used loosely for any thick soup or potage. The village is on the north-east coast of Scotland, where smoked haddock — particularly the pale, naturally wood-smoked variety known as Finnan haddie — is the local specialty. The soup is made by poaching smoked haddock in milk, using the resulting stock as the soup base, and adding potatoes and onion to produce a thick, chowder-like consistency. Avoid bright-yellow dyed haddock; the natural pale variety has a cleaner smoke and a more delicate flavour. Cullen skink was served at a state banquet at Holyrood Palace in 2009.

recipeTools.notes: A large saucepan for the soup.

content.text: Poach the haddock gently in milk rather than boiling it: boiling toughens the fish and makes it grainy. The milk used to poach the fish becomes the base of the soup and carries all the smoke flavour. Mash about a third of the cooked potato into the broth to give the soup its characteristic thick, slightly grainy texture, leaving the rest as chunks.

items.preparation: peeled and diced into 2 cm chunks

content.text: Place the haddock skin-side up in a large saucepan with the milk and bay leaves. Add 300 ml of water. Bring just to a simmer over medium heat, then poach gently for 8 minutes. Remove the fish. Reserve the milk. When the fish is cool enough to handle, flake it into large pieces, discarding the skin and any bones.

Melt the butter in the same (cleaned) pan. Add the onion and cook for 8 minutes over medium heat until very soft but not coloured. Add the diced potato and the reserved poaching milk. Simmer for 15 minutes until the potato is completely tender.

Mash about a third of the potato roughly into the soup to thicken it. Remove the bay leaves. Stir in the cream and then the flaked haddock. Heat through gently without boiling. Season with pepper. Taste before adding salt as the haddock is already salty. Serve in warmed bowls scattered with chopped parsley.
